content:
alex: CI publish job failing on main: `ci/publish-image` -> final step returns 401 when finalizing manifest. saw this right after the Dockerfile rewrite that squashed stages and added `--chown` in a COPY. logs: 'manifest push failed: unauthorized'. Can someone triage?
jordan: ugh. which registry? full job link? :eyes:
alex: registry: registry.redwood-inference.internal/team/runtime, job: https://ci.redwood/12345
infra-bot: [job ci/publish-image #12345] triggered rerun by @alex at 2026-03-15T09:12:30Z
maria: i've seen a similar pattern when inline cache + buildx pushed stale digests — registry returns 401 if the token used for an earlier chunk expired during finalize. try a rerun with cache disabled.
alex: rerun done (no changes) -> still failing. full error snippet: ```
2026-03-15T09:12:41Z stderr: pushing manifest for redwood/runtime:ci-202603...
error: unexpected EOF while uploading layer
response status: 401
body: {"errors":[{"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"token expired"}]}
```
sam: token expired + parallel uploads = race. Are we using credential helper that refreshes tokens per PUT/POST? If not, the long-running kaniko/upload process can hold stale auth.
jordan: also did we change how we compute Content-Length in the squash stage? some registries reject inconsistent lengths and then subsequent finalize returns weird auth errors. Any recent changes to the build pipeline besides Dockerfile?
alex: pipeline change: switched to buildx with inline cache and enabled concurrent layer uploads for speed. No auth helper change.
maria: try a quick check: `skopeo inspect docker://registry.redwood-inference.internal/team/runtime:ci-previous` - does it succeed from the CI runner with same creds?
alex: skopeo inspect -> 401 as well. So it's not just pushing.
sam: can you run one push with env DEBUG_REGISTRY=1 and DISABLE_INLINE_CACHE=1 and attach logs? Also try `REGISTRY_TOKEN_REFRESH=1` (our helper flag) to force credential refresh between requests.
alex: starting a rerun with DISABLE_INLINE_CACHE=1 + DEBUG_REGISTRY. Kicking off now.
jordan: if that fails, bisect plan: run CI on commit before the Dockerfile stage squash (sha: b7a9c1) and then on latest to narrow down; ask infra to run those two in sequence so tokens aren't stale. @infra-bot can we schedule two serial runs?
infra-bot: scheduled: ci/publish-image for sha b7a9c1 (run 12400) then for sha head (run 12401). Notifications will follow.
maria: one-off workaround: force uploads to use single-threaded mode (`UPLOAD_PARALLELISM=1`) to see if the race goes away. If that helps, we know it's concurrency + token TTL.
alex: noted. adding UPLOAD_PARALLELISM=1 to the run. will paste logs when done.
(brief pause)
alex: run 12400 (pre-dockerfile-squash) succeeded. run 12401 (current head) failed with same 401 during manifest finalize.
sam: ok that narrows it to the Dockerfile rewrite or the buildx/inline-cache flip. Try repeating current head but with DISABLE_INLINE_CACHE=1 + UPLOAD_PARALLELISM=1. If that passes, inline-cache + concurrency is culprit.
alex: running that combo now.
(ends)
